title: 2.3.8 Predict Where default Runs
description: Write two switch statements, predicting the output before you run each one, including one where default is written in the middle. Auto-graded.
sourceRef: book 2.3.2: Concepts in Practice: Reading a switch, Q1 and Q2

steps.title: Write a switch and predict
steps.instructions: Create a variable grade set to 'A', 'B', or something else. Before you write the switch, write a comment predicting which line will print. Then write a switch on grade with a case for 'A', a case for 'B', and a default, each ending in break.

steps.title: Write a second switch with default in the middle
steps.instructions: Create a second variable (for example n) set to a number that matches no case. Write a switch where the default label comes BEFORE the last case label, not after it. Before running, write a comment predicting whether default still runs even though it isn't last. Then run it and check.

requirements.title: second switch statement present
requirements.description: Code contains a second switch statement, each switching on a real variable

requirements.title: default written before a case in the second switch
requirements.description: The second switch writes default (with a console.log) before one of its case labels.

requirements.title: at least three breaks
requirements.description: Code contains at least three break statements (the A and B cases of the first switch, and a case in the second).
